text:
Connor O'Brien: runtime-1.22 release coordination thread. Need to lock the “must land” list (profile pack), doc deadlines, and confirm backport policy for 1.21.x/LTS. Please reply here with blockers/concerns.

Connor O'Brien: Proposed dates (PT):
- Code freeze: Wed 2/5 EOD
- RC cut: Thu 2/6 10am
- Hosted canary enablement: Thu 2/6 afternoon (post-SRE signoff)
- GA to Hosted defaults: Mon 2/10 (if canary clean)
- Dedicated: opt-in only for 1.22 (no default flip)

Connor O'Brien: “Must land” PRs for 1.22 (redwood repo):
- #24873 profile pack loader + schema validation + initial H100/L40S defs behind flag
- #24881 selection logic by GPU SKU/driver + override precedence + logs
- #24895 scheduler workload buckets / queue priority guardrails
- #24902 KV cache compaction thresholds + counters
- #24911 H100 attention kernel v3 + fallback rules + kernel_choice metric
- #24935 tag latency hists with profile_id/sku + scheduler_queue_ms
- #24944 config: profile_version pin + customer override guardrails + audit hook
- #24979 rollout flag + kill-switch / rollback path
- #25014 add profile pack version to /health + debug endpoints
- #25037 CI: schema validation step + golden snapshots

Connor O'Brien: Cross-repo “must land” (or we ship without but then we’re blind):
- benchmark-lab #913 (matrix runner persisting profile_version + sha)
- perf-canary #388 (default profile delta checks + Slack notify)
- observability-pack #221 (dashboards: adoption + p95 by profile + kernel fallback panels)
- redwood-docs #511 (internal/external doc draft)
- redwood-helm-charts #144 (Private values + docs)

Connor O'Brien: Docs deadlines: Elliot/Kira can you confirm what you need by when? I want to avoid merging runtime bits without a minimally correct “expected behavior + rollback” page.

Talia Benson: +1. For program mgmt: we also need the go/no-go checklist in the release ticket by Mon 2/3. Connor can you paste this list into the checklist doc once final?

Sahana Iyer: From CI/perf gating side: #25037 is non-negotiable for me. Also want perf-canary #388 wired to block (not just warn) when p99 regression > threshold on mixed bucket. We can start as warn in RC and flip to block after a week, but need agreement.

Sean Gallagher: SRE POV: gating criteria has to include error rate + tail latency + OOM signals. If perf-canary is warn-only at first, then the Hosted canary needs an explicit manual signoff checkpoint (pager coverage). Also please make sure #25014 (debug endpoints) is in before canary, otherwise on-call is blind.

Rafael Mendes: rollout automation: #24979 gives us kill-switch semantics. I’d like it to default OFF in Dedicated/Private and only controlled via fleet config. Also need docs to say exactly what kill-switch reverts (profile pack selection vs individual knobs).

Mateo Alvarez: For runtime: agree on must-lands. I’d add #24958 (fix profile mismatch on model reload across GPU pools) to the required list. That bug is nasty under autoscale.

Connor O'Brien: good catch, adding #24958 to must-land. Anything else in the “can’t ship w/out” bucket?

Hiro Tanaka: kernel side: #24911 is the big one. But if we ship attention v3, we should also ship the fallback counters from that PR (I think they’re already there). If it gets split, don’t drop the telemetry.

Allison Grant: Observability: I’m okay if observability-pack #221 lands slightly after RC cut, but only if the raw metrics/tags are already in runtime (#24935). Without dashboards we can still query, but it slows incident response. Strong preference: dashboards before Hosted canary.

Ethan Park: config/control plane: #24944 introduces profile_version pin. Please ensure the audit log hook is behind the same flag (we had previous cardinality issues). Also we need a clear precedence order in docs: fleet default < Dedicated customer pin < runtime env override(?)

Connor O'Brien: re: precedence, my understanding is:
1) hard compatibility gate (SKU/driver/CUDA) can refuse unsafe selection
2) explicit profile_version pin (Dedicated/Private) if passes guardrails
3) fleet default profile_version (Hosted)
4) runtime built-in fallback (if pack missing) -> baseline conservative settings
We should align wording w/ docs.

Neha Kapoor: Infra note: B200 bring-up is still messy on driver/CUDA. Please do NOT allow silent “best guess” on B200. If B200 nodes exist, runtime should refuse defaults unless profile_version explicitly set and driver baseline matches. (I think #24927 does that but want it verified.)

Connor O'Brien: ack. B200 is “preview” for 1.22, not GA. We’ll keep it gated.

Elliot Price: Docs plan:
- By Tue 2/4 EOD: Confluence pages must be ready for review (overview + expected behavior H100/L40S + rollout/runbook + benchmark protocol)
- By Wed 2/5 noon: final edits in after SRE/Infra review
- By RC cut Thu 2/6: in-repo docs PR (#511) merged OR at least linked from release notes + marked “internal only”
We can work with draft numbers, but need the definitive knobs list + guardrails text by Tue.

Kira Thompson: +1. Also need a short “How to rollback” section with exact commands / config flips for Hosted (feature flag), Dedicated (pin profile_version), Private (Helm values). If those mechanisms change after Tue, docs will churn.

Sean Gallagher: If docs aren’t ready by Tue, we should push canary. Rollout without a tested rollback path is not acceptable.

Connor O'Brien: agreed. Let’s treat docs readiness as a go/no-go gate for Hosted canary.

Talia Benson: Can we also clarify backport policy here? Support asked last time whether profile-only fixes will get backported to 1.21.x.

Connor O'Brien: Backport policy proposal (runtime-1.21.x LTS):
- Yes: safety/correctness fixes (crashes, OOM regressions, incorrect profile selection), schema validation bug fixes, audit/logging that improves triage with low risk.
- No: performance “tuning improvements” unless they address a confirmed regression/incident and have perf-canary evidence.
- “Maybe”: new dashboard panels (generally no backport unless required for incident).
Please react/argue.

Mateo Alvarez: +1. Perf tuning backports are risky. If we do one, it should be behind a flag and default off in LTS.

Sahana Iyer: Works for me, but I want the criteria written: perf regression = p99 up > X% for mixed bucket, or tokens/sec down > Y% at fixed latency. Otherwise it becomes subjective.

Sean Gallagher: +1. Also backports should include a rollback note in release notes + an owner on-call for first 24h after deployment.

Rafael Mendes: Dedicated customers are going to ask for “pin to known-good” more than “backport tuning.” So backporting the pinning UX (if not already in 1.21) could be valuable.

Ethan Park: profile_version pin (#24944) is 1.22. If we want it in 1.21.x, that’s more than a small backport (touches config parsing + audit). I’d prefer not, unless a major customer escalation.

Neha Kapoor: From infra: please don’t backport B200 logic to 1.21.x unless we’re actually running B200 under 1.21 (we’re not planning to).

Allison Grant: Observability backports: low priority unless it fixes an alert false-positive. Prefer keep LTS stable.

Connor O'Brien: Sounds aligned: conservative LTS backports.

ReleaseBot: Reminder: runtime-1.22 RC cut scheduled for 2026-02-06 10:00 PT. Please ensure all required PRs have approvals and passing checks.

Connor O'Brien: Action items:
- Connor: add #24958 to checklist, update release ticket w/ final must-land list + dates
- Elliot/Kira: doc review request list by Mon EOD; tag SRE/Infra reviewers
- Sahana/Allison: confirm perf-canary + dashboards readiness for Thu canary
- Sean/Rafael: confirm kill-switch + rollback runbook language by Tue

Elliot Price: I’ll ping reviewers today. Expect SRE to ask for explicit “what metrics are gates” table.

Sean Gallagher: yep. Please include thresholds for: p95/p99 latency, scheduler_queue_ms, error rate, kernel_fallback_rate, OOM count, fragmentation estimate. Even if some are “watch-only,” list them.

Connor O'Brien: ok. I’ll keep this thread open until RC cut. Post here when each must-land PR is merged / blocked.

Talia Benson: Tracking in the epic as well. If anything slips past Wed freeze, call it out early.

Connor O'Brien: (later) status update: #24873 merged, #24881 in final review, #24895 rerunning benchmarks. Still waiting on perf-canary #388 to merge.

Sahana Iyer: perf-canary #388 should merge today; last change was to reduce noise from region variance. Will post once green.

Allison Grant: dashboards PR #221 is ready for final approval once metric names stabilize. Please don’t rename scheduler_queue_ms again :)

Connor O'Brien: noted. No more metric rename churn unless we find a correctness issue.

Sean Gallagher: once #25014 is merged, please drop the /debug snippet in #oncall-notes so we can validate during canary.

Connor O'Brien: will do.
